record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.context_brief: Infinite surviving components in lattice WARMs
record.original_question: For a WARM on the integer lattice graph G=Z^d with d >= 2 and reinforcement exponent alpha > 1, can one choose a bounded firing-rate function p that is not bounded away from zero so that the set of surviving edges contains an infinite connected component almost surely or with positive probability? If such an infinite surviving component can occur, is it unique?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 14 Do there exist a bounded (but not bounded away from 0) function p, d ≥ 2, and α > 1 for which the WARM on the graph G = Z d almost surely (or indeed with positive probability) contains an infinite connected component of surviving edges? If such a component exists, is it unique?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d\ge 2$ be the standard nearest-neighbor integer lattice graph, with vertex set $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and edges between vertices at Euclidean distance $1$. Fix a reinforcement exponent $\alpha>1$ and a function $p:\mathbb{Z}^d\to(0,\infty)$ that is bounded above (i.e. $\sup_v p(v)<\infty$) but not bounded away from zero (i.e. $\inf_v p(v)=0$). Define the Weighted Adaptive Reinforcement Model (WARM) on $G$ as follows. Each vertex $v$ has an independent Poisson clock of rate $p(v)$. Every edge $e$ carries a weight $W_e(t)$ initialized at $W_e(0)=1$. When the clock at $v$ rings at time $t$, one edge $e$ incident to $v$ is selected with probability
$$\frac{W_e(t-)^{\alpha}}{\sum_{e'\ni v} W_{e'}(t-)^{\alpha}},$$
and its weight is incremented by $1$. An edge $e$ is called surviving if it is selected infinitely often almost surely; equivalently, $W_e(t)\to\infty$ as $t\to\infty$. Let $\mathcal{E}_\infty$ denote the (random) set of surviving edges, viewed as a subgraph of $G$.

(a) Do there exist $d\ge 2$, $\alpha>1$, and a choice of bounded firing-rate function $p$ as above (not bounded away from $0$) such that, with positive probability (or almost surely), $\mathcal{E}_\infty$ contains an infinite connected component?

(b) Whenever such an infinite component exists, is it almost surely unique?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in the literature on WARM (weighted activation reinforcement models). Related results show that on regular trees infinite surviving components can occur for sufficiently large α with non-uniform (decaying) firing rates, and that on Z^d in the very strong reinforcement regime no percolation occurs when rates are bounded away from 0 and ∞. No source found resolves the case of Z^d with bounded but vanishing rates for general α>1; the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Absence of WARM percolation in the very strong reinforcement regime
status_evidence.snippet: For α sufficiently large the surviving subgraph does not percolate; existence of infinite components on Z^d for α>1 is not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: Related WARM percolation results on Z^d are partial and do not resolve the bounded-non-vanishing rate case.

status_evidence.title: Infinite WARM graphs III: strong reinforcement regime
status_evidence.snippet: For α>2 infinite surviving components exist on certain trees with firing rates decaying away from a root.
status_evidence.claim: Infinite components are known on trees with vanishing firing rates, suggesting analogous Z^d question remains open.
